document.description: ACIAD3523 encodes MesD, a compact catalytic-barrel methionine synthase associated with the neighboring MesX protein. Native Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 genetics supports methionine synthesis without added cobalamin. The protein lacks the N-terminal folate-binding barrel of canonical MetE. MesD-family evidence supports sulfur methyl transfer to homocysteine, with conserved catalytic zinc coordination; the physiological methyl donor and purified ADP1 reaction remain unidentified. Aerobic dependence was established in comparative MesD/MesX complementation rather than in an isolated ADP1 enzyme assay.

review.reason: Native ADP1 methionine auxotrophy and the exact MesD identity support the final homocysteine-methylation role. The original electronic EC/family mapping incorrectly fixes the methyl donor. S-methyltransferase activity retains the supported chemistry without inventing the physiological donor or treating S. koreensis complementation as a purified ADP1 assay.

document.description: ACIAD3524 encodes MesX, a member of the former DUF1852 family required for the MesD-associated, cobalamin-independent methionine-synthesis route in Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1. Native deletion causes methionine auxotrophy and expression of ACIAD3524 restores prototrophy. Related MesD/MesX pairs support aerobic methionine synthesis in heterologous complementation, but the molecular action of MesX remains unresolved. Methyl-donor generation or transfer is a hypothesis; independent oxidase activity, a bound methyl carrier, and a stable MesD–MesX catalytic complex have not been established.

document.description: cbdbA481 encodes the compact MesB-type methionine synthase of Dehalococcoides mccartyi CBDB1. Purified untagged recombinant protein transfers a methyl group from methylcobalamin to homocysteine, forming methionine in anoxic assays. The enzyme lacks the folate-binding half of canonical MetE and does not use methyl-tetrahydrofolate triglutamate in the tested reaction. The physiological corrinoid donor remains unidentified: transfer from the AcsCD corrinoid iron-sulfur protein is a proposed route, not a demonstrated native transfer reaction. The protein does not rescue an E. coli metE deletion under the tested complementation conditions.

document.description: LuxS is a cytosolic S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase that releases L-homocysteine and 4,5-dihydroxy-2,3-pentadione in the Pfs/LuxS arm of the activated methyl cycle. document.description: MetK is the cytosolic S-adenosylmethionine synthetase of Escherichia coli K-12. Its functional homotetramer contains intersubunit active sites that join methionine to ATP and hydrolyze the released tripolyphosphate before product release. Catalysis uses divalent metal ions and is activated by potassium. MetK supplies SAM for methyl-group transfer and other SAM-dependent chemistry and participates directly in methionine cycling. Tagged-cell studies reveal both diffuse cytoplasmic signal and focal distributions.

document.description: MmuM, formerly YagD, is a zinc-dependent homocysteine S-methyltransferase of Escherichia coli K-12. It transfers a methyl group from S-methylmethionine to homocysteine, yielding two methionine molecules, and enables utilization of imported S-methylmethionine when folate-dependent methionine synthesis is unavailable. Purified MmuM also accepts SAM as a donor and selenium-containing acceptors. SAM-dependent activity has been linked to use of damaged SAM stereoisomers in distinct experimental contexts. These reactions do not by themselves establish a complete endogenous S-methylmethionine cycle.

document.description: CheR is the chemoreceptor methyltransferase of the Escherichia coli chemotaxis adaptation system, a 286-aa soluble S-adenosylmethionine-dependent enzyme with a small N-terminal helical domain and a larger C-terminal Rossmann-like SAM-binding domain carrying a beta-subdomain. CheR transfers methyl groups from S-adenosylmethionine to specific glutamyl residues in the cytoplasmic domains of methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (Tar, Tsr, Trg, Tap), forming glutamyl 5-methyl esters (EC 2.1.1.80). It docks on the C-terminal NWETF pentapeptide of the high-abundance receptors Tar and Tsr, a site distinct from the methylation sites, which tethers the enzyme to receptor arrays and allows it to methylate neighbouring receptors, including low-abundance receptors that lack the pentapeptide. Opposing CheB-mediated demethylation, CheR methylation resets receptor signaling output during sustained stimulation (sensory adaptation); cheR mutants cannot adapt, swim smoothly and are non-chemotactic.
